clue.text: Piper, foreman of the crew

definitions.meaning: a ship's officer who sounds the whistle or pipe to call the hands
the petty officer in charge of a ship's deck hands and rigging

explanation.definitionFit: A bosun blows the call on a pipe and supervises the deckhands, so both senses fit the ship's petty officer.

clue.text: Flower many found in flatter surroundings

indicators.note: found in says the word for many is placed inside the phrase for flatter

parts.note: to flatter someone is to butter them up
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: A great many of something turn up surrounded by flatter ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like an adjective about level ground, but it is the verb; 'surroundings' backs up 'found in', saying the flattering phrase encloses the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a common yellow meadow plant in bloom.

clue.text: Profession of a fellow in Jordan

parts.note: a profession is a declaration, as in 'I am', so the verb of avowal
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man in Jordan declares what job he does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' looks like a job, but here it is an avowal: the fellow professes 'I am a man', giving AM plus MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city located in Jordan.

clue.text: … and not this chap from France.

parts.note: nor is the conjunction meaning and not
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a repeal, and not this Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 4 Down's surface, but the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Normans came from Normandy in northern France.

clue.text: Palm-tree for a parrot

definitions.meaning: a tropical American palm shares its name with the bird
a large, brightly coloured long-tailed tropical bird

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tropical American palm species and a large long-tailed tropical bird.

clue.text: Complaint of a female graduate

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
a lady is a female

explanation.surface: A woman with a degree makes a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the sense of an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Island crop for goat

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: An island's harvest is grown to feed a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign is symbolised by a sea-goat.

clue.text: We let her appear in the scene

indicators.note: appear in says the word her shows up inside the word we

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We allow her to come on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' is only a link word; 'scene' is defined by the noun sense, as in 'the where and when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Where, as a noun, is the place or setting in which something happens.

clue.text: What pride makes of an acrobat?

definitions.text: What pride makes of an acrobat?

parts.words: What pride makes of an acrobat?
parts.note: pride goes before a fall, so it turns a person into one who falls; an acrobat who does falls and somersaults

explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat who performs somersaults and falls, and proverbially pride makes one fall.

clue.text: Sapper pales anew, suffering this

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers

indicators.note: anew means the letters of pales are made over afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: An army engineer goes pale again, as when sickness returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' signals the rearrangement of 'pales'; the sapper is the Royal Engineers convention, and the definition leans on the surface, where a relapse is what the soldier suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness that a patient undergoes after apparent recovery.

clue.text: Mental weariness, having crossed Channel

parts.note: a listless boredom described by a word that came to English from France across the Channel

explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword for listless boredom, borrowed into English from across the Channel.

clue.text: Old man's archaic method of ringing the changes

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a grandfather, as the clue's 'archaic' says
a named method used in English church change ringing

explanation.definitionFit: It is both an old word for grandfather and the name of a standard bell-ringing method.

clue.text: In the plant it produces swiftness

indicators.note: In says the word it is placed inside the name of the plant

parts.note: celery is a salad plant

explanation.surface: Something in a plant makes it grow fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for speed or quickness.

clue.text: Rock music's sound under the trees

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, places the sound below the trees

parts.note: limes are linden trees
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Rock music is heard beneath the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary stone made largely of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: Long for one in Strathclyde

parts.note: Long is the name of a Scottish sea inlet in the Strathclyde region, so it is an example of the lake word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like the verb to yearn, but it is the proper name of a sea inlet in western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a lake or sea inlet, of which Long is one.

clue.text: Wonderland court was certainly not so cruel

definitions.text: Wonderland court was certainly not so cruel

parts.words: Wonderland court was certainly not so cruel
parts.note: the court of the Queen of Hearts in Alice in Wonderland was full of hearts, so could not be lacking them, though it was in fact cruel

explanation.definitionFit: Heartless means cruel, and a court ruled by the Queen of Hearts was literally full of hearts.

clue.text: What a relief this was in 1900

definitions.text: What a relief this was in 1900

parts.words: What a relief this was in 1900
parts.note: the besieged South African town relieved in May 1900 during the Boer War, sparking celebrations in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The relief of the besieged South African town in 1900 caused wild rejoicing in Britain.

clue.text: "Oh soft of the still midnight" (Keats)

parts.note: the opening line of Keats's sonnet To Sleep, with the missing word to be filled in

explanation.definitionFit: Keats addresses sleep as a preserver of the dead, the word filling the gap in his sonnet's first line.

clue.text: Some coypu, maybe, or a large cat

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a coypu, perhaps, or a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'or', which is only the link between wordplay and definition, so it is dropped here.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a big American feline.

clue.text: Home of a diabolical marsupial

parts.note: the island state where the devil, a carnivorous pouched mammal, lives

explanation.definitionFit: The Australian island state is the native home of the devil, a fierce pouched mammal.

clue.text: More than one of Verdi's characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of Verdi's are taken as letters and reordered

explanation.surface: Several figures from the operas of Verdi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like the people in an opera, but it means letters: those of VERDIS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old word for several or various.

clue.text: Its maltreatment did so fluster Tweedledum

definitions.text: Its maltreatment did so fluster Tweedledum

parts.words: Its maltreatment did so fluster Tweedledum
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass, Tweedledum is furious that his new toy has been spoilt

explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's story, Tweedledum's spoilt toy noisemaker provokes the battle with Tweedledee.

clue.text: Send down for making acute stir

indicators.note: making means the letters of acute stir are made into something new

explanation.surface: A student is expelled for causing a big fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to suspend a student from university for a time.

clue.text: Absolute competitor

parts.note: Captain Absolute is a character in Sheridan's comedy named after competitors in love

explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute' looks like an adjective, but it is Captain Absolute from Sheridan's play The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is an opponent, and Captain Absolute is one of Sheridan's title figures.

clue.text: Slang for a sovereign understood

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, a sovereign
got means understood, as in 'I got it'

explanation.surface: A colloquial word for a monarch is grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or cant of a particular group.

clue.text: Information about style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind or category of artistic work.

clue.text: Not live broadcast, though vivid

indicators.note: broadcast means the letters of not live are scattered and resown

explanation.surface: A recorded rather than live programme that is still colourful.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent colours are intense, garish and vivid.

clue.text: Huge fellows in semi-drunken state

indicators.note: in says the fellows go inside the rearranged letters
drunken means the letters of semi are staggering about

parts.note: fellows are men

explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges the four letters of 'semi', and 'in' places the fellows in the middle of that jumble; 'state' is only a link word.

clue.text: But this castle's not in' West Yorkshire

definitions.text: But this castle's not in' West Yorkshire

parts.words: But this castle's not in' West Yorkshire
parts.note: the castle of this name is in Kent, though a big city of the same name is in West Yorkshire

explanation.definitionFit: The city is in West Yorkshire, but the castle of that name stands in Kent.

clue.text: With which four young oysters were consumed

definitions.text: With which four young oysters were consumed

parts.words: With which four young oysters were consumed
parts.note: in Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, four young oysters hurried up all keen for the treat, and were then eaten
